title: The self made of breath
hookLine: the demons could pierce the mind but shattered on the breath, and the Taittiriya finds a self made of each
carry: inside the body, breath; inside breath, mind
last: ANNAMAYA — THE SELF MADE OF FOOD.

lines: THEY PIERCE SPEECH, SIGHT, HEARING, MIND.
cards: Remember the gods and the demons in the Brihadaranyaka? The gods sent out their powers to chant for them, one at a time. Speech went, and the demons pierced it with evil; that's why we say things we shouldn't.
Smell, sight, hearing and the mind were all pierced the same way. Then the gods sent the breath in the mouth. The demons rushed at it and scattered, like a clod of earth thrown at a stone.
Today the Taittiriya puts breath and mind in their places, inside you.

teach.h: INSIDE FOOD, A SELF MADE OF BREATH.
teach.b: After the self made of food, the text says: different from this, and inside it, is another self, made of breath. Pranamaya. The outer self is filled by this one, and this one too has the shape of a person.

teach.h: THE BREATH-SELF, DRAWN AS A BIRD.
teach.b: The text draws the breath-self like a bird. Prana, the in-breath, is its head. Vyana, the breath that spreads through the body, is one wing.
Apana, the down-going breath, is the other. Space is its body, and the earth is its tail. And it says why breath matters: prano hi bhutanam ayuh.
Breath is the life-span of all beings. Gods, people and animals all breathe after it. Then the text goes in again.

teach.h: INSIDE BREATH, A SELF MADE OF MIND.
teach.b: Inside the breath-self is a self made of mind. Manomaya. And this bird is drawn out of scripture.
The Yajur Veda is its head, the Rig Veda and Sama Veda its wings, teaching its body, the hymns of the Atharvans its tail.

teach.h: A MIND SHAPED BY SACRED WORDS.
teach.b: Many teachers read this as: the mind is shaped by the sacred words a person learns and carries.
Put the two together, and you have the reason many Hindus give for a practice they still keep before puja or meditation: pranayama, breath practice.
Yoga teachers read it as work on the layer between the body and the mind, the same breath the demons could not stain: steady the breath, and the mind riding on it steadies too.
And then the text points inward once more: inside this one, another self. That's tomorrow.

how: Many Hindus learn the Taittiriya's five layers through Vedanta study and yoga teaching, where breath practice (pranayama) is described as working on the pranamaya layer between body and mind.

o: a spirit that leaves the body at night
the air around us, outside the body
prana: life-span of all beings, a self within

games.q: the breath-self and the mind-self — tap the pairs.

s: in the Brihadaranyaka, the demons pierced the breath just as they pierced the mind
they pierced speech, sight, hearing and mind, but on the breath in the mouth they scattered like clay hitting a stone.
in the text, only people live by breath
prano hi bhutanam ayuh: breath is the life-span of beings; gods, people and animals breathe after it.
the text draws the mind-self out of the Vedas
the Yajur Veda is its head, the Rig and Sama its wings.

games.q: you've just learned the self made of food. the Taittiriya says there's another self. where does it say to look?
o: outside the body, in the sky.
inside the food-self: a self made of breath.
nowhere. the body is all there is.
games.why: different from the food-self and inside it is a self made of breath, which fills the outer one and has the shape of a person.

practice: Sit tall, the self made of food. Breathe in slowly through the nose for a count of four, and out for a count of six: a simple pranayama, the kind many Hindus do for a few rounds before puja.
If you pray, let each out-breath carry a soft Om. If you don't, let it carry the count. Feel the breath fill the body from the inside, belly, ribs, throat.
Then notice the mind riding on the breath, a word, a plan, a tune, and let the slow breath carry it.

wordCard.voice: Breath. Prana, the life-span of beings, which in the Taittiriya forms a whole self inside the body, with the self made of mind inside it.

orig.note: Sanskrit prāṇamaya: prāṇa, breath, + maya, made of. the second self in Taittiriya 2.2.

carryVoice: Your line: inside the body, breath; inside breath, mind. Week fifty-six: desire, not this, fullness, truth and dharma, the guest, food, and breath. Day three hundred ninety-two, done.

sources.ref: Taittiriya Upanishad 2.2–2.3 (the self made of breath; the self made of mind)
